mainEntity.name: Should I expand my home outward with a ground-floor addition or build upward?

acceptedAnswer.text: A ground-floor bump-out extends outward onto your yard, while a second-story addition builds upward on top of your existing structure. Ground-level extensions require foundation work and yard area, but they cause less disruption to your existing living quarters during framing. Second-story additions preserve your yard space but require evaluating the existing foundation to ensure it can support vertical loads, often requiring temporary relocation during roof removal and structural reinforcement. Bay City Remodeling & Bathrooms reviews your structural layout and lot lines during planning to determine which direction works best for your home.
